_comment_1: ATOMIC GRANULARITY ONLY. One row per requirement, not per chapter. A 14-day project should produce on the order of 100 rows. If your row count is implausibly low for project age, the loop will self-terminate before the product is good. This is the Flatline failure mode.
_comment_2: Allowed status values: not_started | partial | done | deprecated. Every row should carry implementationRefs and testRefs once status >= partial. followupRefs link to F-NNN entries in FOLLOWUPS.md. A row marked status=deprecated stays in the ledger for institutional memory but no implementation or tests are owed; add a note in the row explaining what removed it from scope (slice id, Q-NNN resolution, etc.).

rows.requirement: Timeline persistence: actions performed during a time period are recorded and replay as a permanent past instance whenever another instance witnesses that period from outside it.
Past instances replay recorded input frame-exact and cannot be altered, only worked around or physically redirected.
Traveling through a portal does not erase the prior timeline; the entered instance continues to exist as a recorded instance in the timeline left behind.
System enforces the no-paradox invariant: a player cannot prevent themselves from having done something they already did.
Portals have fixed locations and fixed destinations; a given door always leads to the same other time.
An unvisited future contains no recorded events and no instances; a time period only contains events once an instance has entered it.
Instance generation numbering tracks generations from the original spawn (You1, You-1, You-2, ...).
Player input always controls the most recently spawned active instance.
A lit door is enterable and sends the player to the door's fixed destination time.
A dark door is a spawn-only exit; instances emerge from it and the player cannot enter.
Door lit-versus-dark state is computed from arriving instances in the recorded timeline, not stored as a discoverable variable.
Act 1 cinematic at 12:00: two figures drag a knocked-out body through the North door to the center of the room, then fade to black.
Act 1 spawn at 5:00: the player stands in the center of the room, with North and West dark and South and East lit.
Door destinations from 5:00: South leads to 12:00 and East leads to 6:00.
6:00 timeline state: the room is empty, only the West door is lit, and the West door leads back to 5:00.
Act 2 first loop: traveling East then West produces a You-1 instance who replays You1's path, walks West, and disappears.
Act 2 second loop: knocking out You-1 on return to 5:00 and dragging the body East to 6:00 produces a You-2 instance who wakes and knocks out You1.
Act 3 setup: repeating the Act 2 sequence positions a knocked-out instance at 6:00 and the player waits for the other instance to wake.
Act 3 chase beat: running toward the West door while another instance chases pulls both instances through to 5:00 in the same frame.
Act 3 team-up beat: the two instances at 5:00 coordinate to knock out the 5:00 instance.
Act 3 mirror beat: dragging the knocked-out instance South to 12:00 and placing the body in the center of the room mirrors the Act 1 cinematic.
Act 3 second knockout: the player knocks out the instance brought from 6:00 inside the 12:00 timeline.
Act 3 escape: with no replay-instance staffing the North door cinematic, the North door at 12:00 is open and running through completes the level.
Beat dependency enforcement: acts cannot be executed out of order, and Act 3 requires the timeline state produced by Act 2.
Hard reset is available in the pause menu and returns the simulation to a clean Act 1 state.
Player spawn is keyboard-controllable in the room at 5:00.
Four doors render in the scene, one per wall.
Lit-versus-dark visual state of each door correctly reflects portal availability per the time travel rules.
Room color tints across a warm-to-cool spectrum over time.
Past instances tint to the room color at the time they last traveled, providing a visible timestamp.
The active player instance shows a subtle floor ring underfoot.
Thought-bubble icons appear above past instances before key actions (door enter, fight, sleep).
Knockouts produce ragdoll physics on the receiving instance.
Unconscious bodies can be picked up by the player.
Unconscious bodies can be dragged across the room while held.
Unconscious bodies can be thrown through doors and travel to the door's destination time.
Demo build deploys to web with no install required.
Demo build loads in under 10 seconds on a typical broadband connection.
Demo build runs at 60fps on a 2020-era laptop.
Demo build supports the full Act 1 to Act 3 puzzle without crashes or timeline desync.
